newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Holyman buys into Catalina ferry service.
newsitem.headline: Holyman buys into Catalina ferry service.

text.p: Shipping group Holyman Ltd said on Tuesday it had established Holyman Catalina Agencies LLC to provide agency services to the Catalina Cruises passenger ferry service, operating four ferries between Long Beach and Catalina Island in California.
Holyman said Catalina Cruises caters to local residents and to day-trippers and holiday makers for the service to Catalina Island, about 40 kms from Long Beach.
It serves the Catalina Island ports of Avalon and Two Harbours.

The existing vessels are owned by Catalina Clipper LLC, a U.S. registered company in which Holyman holds a 20 percent interest. The remaining 80 percent interest and 20 percent of the shares in Holyman Catalina Agencies LLC are owned by local ferry operators.
Holyman's investment in the operation is about A$2.0 million.
"Holyman Catalina Agencies is a new company that will not materially contribute to the 1997 results of Holyman," Holyman said.
"It is expected to make a positive contribution in 1998, when Catalina Cruises, with the assistance of Holyman, intends to introduce high speed passenger ferries, replacing current vessels," it said.
Holyman shares were steady at A$3.25 at 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT).
